sections.html:
A cash purchase is the quickest exit in Bridgeton, since no lender appraisal or repair haggling slows it down. Listing opens the door to more buyers but adds showings, inspections and the city's resale form. A sale without an agent lands between the two and carries the same certificate and recording work.

Bridgeton has 28,307 residents on 6.23 square miles of land, and most blocks mix single-family houses, doubles and small rentals.

Bridgeton is a renter-heavy city with modest values. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $145,500, rent is $1,340, and only 36.4% of the 7,481 households own. Median household income is $55,781. Many sellers here are landlords or heirs rather than long-term single-family owners.

The city sits on the tidal Cohansey River and is the Cumberland County seat, in three sections: Northside, Southside and Hillside. Philadelphia is about an hour away, Wilmington about 50 minutes, and Atlantic City and Cape May roughly an hour. A low entry price and a reachable job market draw investors, which is one reason cash offers are common.

  • Victorian and Federal-era houses near the downtown core often need roof, porch and plumbing work.
  • Many blocks of "doubles" were built as working-class housing and are now often rentals.
  • Occupied rentals can be sold with tenants in place, but the buyer will ask for the rental registration and inspection record.

sections.h2: Does the historic district affect a sale?
sections.html:
For a large share of the city it can. The Bridgeton Historic District covers about a quarter of the city and includes more than 2,000 properties ranging from early Federal buildings to 1920s construction.

If your house is inside the district, ask the city's Historic District Administrative Officer, who works alongside Code Enforcement, what review applies to exterior work before you replace windows, siding or porches ahead of a sale. Buyers who plan renovations will ask the same question.

Routes 49 and 77 and County Route 552 are the main roads, and NJ Transit's 410 bus runs between Bridgeton and Philadelphia. Bridgeton Public Schools runs eight schools for pre-kindergarten through grade 12, and students can also apply to the Cumberland County Technical Education Center in Millville. Mention the bus line and school options in your listing.

The Code Enforcement Office enforces the 2015 International Property Maintenance Code and also handles home sales. On the sale of any property in the city, a resale Certificate of Property Compliance (CPC) form must be filled out and filed with the office. Ask about inspection timing early, because a failed inspection means a notice, repairs and a re-inspection before a certificate issues. The Housing and Code department is at 181 E. Commerce Street.

Landlords carry extra steps. Every rental unit must be registered each year by March 1, whether vacant or occupied, and must pass inspection before tenants move in or whenever occupancy changes. The city also has a rent leveling ordinance, Ordinance 25-28, which matters to anyone buying or selling an occupied building. Tree removal above set trunk sizes needs an application too.

sections.h2: Property taxes for a Bridgeton seller
sections.html:
Bridgeton's tax load is heavy relative to its home values, which is a common reason owners want out. Ask the tax collector for the current rate before you quote a monthly carrying cost to a buyer.

The tax collector bills property tax in four installments due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1. The same office collects water, sewer and the solid waste charge, listed at $150 for residents and $90 for seniors. Unpaid balances can attach to the sale, so ask for a payoff or statement before closing.

  • Assessment appeals go to the Cumberland County Board of Taxation, 2475 S. Delsea Drive, Vineland, (856) 453-7425, by April 1 or 45 days after notices are mailed, whichever is later, or May 1 after a municipal-wide revaluation.
  • Assessments above $1,000,000 may be filed directly with the State Tax Court.
  • Senior, disabled and veteran deductions are $250 each and require an application to the assessor.

Many Bridgeton sales involve an estate or a relative, and New Jersey's Realty Transfer Fee has exemptions that fit those cases. Deeds that skip the fee include a parent giving title to a child, one spouse to another, an estate representative passing the house to an heir under a will or intestacy, and a transfer recorded within 90 days after a divorce decree. A seller claiming an exemption files Form RTF-1 with the deed.

An ordinary sale is different: the seller owes the fee at recording, calculated per $500 of the price. On a sale of $150,000 or less, the schedule for deals not over $350,000 starts at $2.00 per $500, so the fee on a typical Bridgeton price is modest compared with the repair cost of an older house.

If you inherited the house, a deed from the executor to you is exempt, but your later sale to a buyer is a regular conveyance. Plan for the fee at recording and ask your attorney to confirm which form applies.

Once you accept an offer, file the resale CPC form with Code Enforcement and book the inspection. Fix anything on the notice, pay the $18 re-inspection if needed, and keep the certificate for the closing file. Ask the tax collector for a statement of taxes, water, sewer and the solid waste charge so no balance follows the sale. If tenants live in the house, gather the unit registration and rent records for the buyer. Your attorney then schedules the closing, the deed is recorded and the seller's fee is paid at recording.

Landlords selling a building with several units should also set aside time for the rent leveling rules. Pull each lease, list the current rents and confirm that every unit's yearly registration is on file, because a buyer's attorney will ask for all of it before the contract becomes final. An older house with open repair notices from the city will move faster if you clear those notices first.

faqs.q: Do I need an inspection to sell my house in Bridgeton?
faqs.a: The city requires a resale Certificate of Property Compliance form to be filed with Code Enforcement on the sale of any property. Call the Housing and Code department at 856-455-3230 to schedule and ask what the inspector checks.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bridgeton house with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Keep the unit registered (due each March 1) and have the current Certificate of Property Compliance and rent records ready, because the buyer takes the property subject to the city's rent leveling ordinance.

faqs.q: How much is the annual rental registration in Bridgeton?
faqs.a: It costs $45 per unit if filed by March 1 and $75 per unit after that date. The registration renewal also covers the rental certificate fees.

faqs.q: Where do I appeal my Bridgeton tax assessment?
faqs.a: Appeal to the Cumberland County Board of Taxation in Vineland at (856) 453-7425, by April 1 or 45 days from the mailing of notices, whichever is later. Properties assessed over $1,000,000 can go straight to the State Tax Court.

faqs.q: Is the realty transfer fee owed if I inherited the house and sell it?
faqs.a: The fee applies to the sale deed. A deed from an executor to an heir is exempt, but the later sale to a buyer is a regular conveyance, so plan for the seller's fee at recording.
